title: Cost And Payment Controls
document_title: SSX Master Cost and Payment Control Activities

items.text: What cost is involved? | Budget, estimate, commitment, invoice, change, allowance, contingency, stored material, payment or forecast
cells: Budget, estimate, commitment, invoice, change, allowance, contingency, stored material, payment or forecast

items.text: Who owns it? | Owner, contractor, subcontractor, supplier, consultant, lender, insurer or surety
cells: Owner, contractor, subcontractor, supplier, consultant, lender, insurer or surety

items.text: What scope does it cover? | WBS, cost code, CSI division, contract package, location, system or change
cells: WBS, cost code, CSI division, contract package, location, system or change

items.text: When is it required? | Budget date, commitment date, billing cutoff, review date, funding date or payment date
cells: Budget date, commitment date, billing cutoff, review date, funding date or payment date

items.text: What supports it? | Contract, purchase order, quantity, invoice, delivery ticket, payroll, schedule progress, inspection or approval
cells: Contract, purchase order, quantity, invoice, delivery ticket, payroll, schedule progress, inspection or approval

items.text: What must approve it? | Project manager, cost manager, architect, owner, lender, auditor or other contract authority
cells: Project manager, cost manager, architect, owner, lender, auditor or other contract authority

items.text: What could hold payment? | Missing backup, disputed scope, deficient work, incomplete closeout, lien waiver, insurance, retainage or funding
cells: Missing backup, disputed scope, deficient work, incomplete closeout, lien waiver, insurance, retainage or funding

items.text: How is it closed? | Reconciled commitment, approved payment, final waiver, released retainage, final audit and archived records
cells: Reconciled commitment, approved payment, final waiver, released retainage, final audit and archived records

items.text: Publish the complete billing calendar at project kickoff.
Move dates falling on weekends or holidays to the contract-defined business day.
Require subcontractors to forecast through month end without billing unsupported work.
Verify projected work again at month end and correct the next application when needed.
Do not bill unapproved changes as approved contract value.
Require stored-material invoices, proof of payment, insurance, photographs and location records.
Require lower-tier waivers when the contract or risk procedure calls for them.
Match every waiver’s legal entity, amount and through-date to the associated payment.
Never request an unconditional waiver before the corresponding funds have cleared.
Identify disputed or withheld amounts in writing while processing undisputed amounts.
Track architect review, owner approval, lender funding, contractor receipt and downstream payment separately.
Coordinate prompt-payment and lien-waiver procedures with project-specific legal requirements.
Include approved amount in owner billing
Obtain bond or letter of credit when required
Convert stored material to installed work
Confirm statutory timing with project counsel or requirements
Release payment only under approved procedure
Place payment hold for expired documents
Reconcile credit card and petty cash
Obtain consent of surety when required
Installed and accepted work → progress approval
Approved change → revised budget and commitment
Final waivers and reconciliation → final payment
Link payment activities to observable, accepted progress.
Track billing cutoffs, reviews, funding and payment as separate dates.
Separate budget, commitment, actual cost, accrual and forecast.
Keep pending changes visible without treating them as approved.
Require documented authorization before transferring funds.
Prevent duplicate billing of stored and installed materials.
Track lien waivers, insurance and bonds as payment prerequisites.
Reconcile schedule progress with billed progress.
Forecast general conditions when completion moves.
Close each commitment before final project financial closure.
